decisions_log.decision: Definition of Ready — approve (self, autonomy). 2 stories READY.
decisions_log.notes: US-B63-1 (modifications table bounded) and US-B63-2 (checklist table bounded) both READY, each with behavior-level acceptance observable through the shipped surface. The defect was MEASURED before any spec text existed (C-35/C-39): an execution probe ran the real generate_project_report over real VariantExecutionResult fixtures and re-read the written .md from disk — N entries -> exactly N rows in BOTH tables at every N tested, 20 000 -> 3 291 816 B = 1.57x the 2 MiB budget. THE FINDING THAT RAISES THIS ABOVE HYGIENE: the document prints 'report size cap: 2097152 bytes' while being 1.57x over it — the truncation marker fires from the hexdump path while the tables that actually blew the budget are never checked. In an evidentiary document a truncation notice that fires while the bound is violated is worse than no bound. TWO BACKLOG CLAIMS CORRECTED AGAINST DISK: (a) 'charge them to _ByteBudget' — they ARE already charged, emit() calls budget.consume() on every section; the missing half is the CHECK, budget.fits() is consulted only inside _hexdump_section, so the budget is accounted and never enforced; (b) the '~208 MB at 100k rows' figure is the pathological regime — measured per-entry cost is 163.6 B realistic (63-char A2L symbol) vs 610.9 B pathological (512-char, the REPORT_CELL_CHARS ceiling), a 3.7x spread, so the budget blows at ~12 700 vs ~3 400 entries. THAT SPREAD IS THE DESIGN DATUM: a fixed row cap is predictable and per-variant fair but cannot bound bytes; the byte budget bounds bytes but is not fair across variants. Cap shape deliberately NOT decided at Phase 0 — ruled in Phase 1 by executing both candidates (C-39), not by taste. OUT of scope, recorded not dropped: the variant-count axis is separately unbounded (no MAX_VARIANTS anywhere in s19_app/, grepped) and affects every per-variant section -> new BACKLOG carry. PROBE SELF-CORRECTION recorded: the first run reported chk_rows=-1 because the checklist heading is emitted as a Mode-B code span (#### Checklist: `chk.json`) and the predicate searched for the bare form — the predicate was wrong, not the artifact. Third occurrence in three batches of the standing un-encoded candidate P-3 (assert the emitted encoding); caught only because the probe returned an IMPOSSIBLE value (-1) rather than a plausible under-count.

THE DESIGN DID NOT ACHIEVE THE BATCH'S OWN THESIS: simulated post-fix at TWO variants the document measured 2 918 330 B = 1.39x budget WITH THE SIZE-CAP MARKER FIRING — and two variants is the ordinary case, the module exists to compare variants. MY OWN REFRAMING WAS REFUTED: 'the tables are an index, _hexdump_section is the evidence' was mine, I pushed it, the Phase-1 architect made it load-bearing, and measurement (parsing the hexdump back into an address->byte map) shows it FALSE for 3 of the 4 bounded cells — applied.after_bytes 200/200 recoverable, applied.before_bytes 0/200, skipped.after_bytes 0, check.expected_bytes 0. LLR-091.3 obliged the code to PRINT 'full bytes in the Memory regions section', a false statement, in the batch whose thesis is that documents must not assert what they don't honour. I asserted it from the SHAPE of the code and never executed it. Other blockers: the at-cap boundary was a PHANTOM (no node had a fixture at M == CAP; the '>=' mutation emits a spurious 'TRUNCATED: 0 of 500' and survives all 24 nodes); the catalog validated the WITHDRAWN in-cell indicator so a CORRECT implementation would fail AT-172; R-TUI-079/080/081 are LIVE batch-48 ids; no qa TC named an architect LLR so the US->HLR->LLR->TC chain marked OK does not close; the only at-cap node was marked slow while tui-ci runs -m 'not slow', so the merge gate would never have executed it. WHAT SURVIVED: the D-15 option-(b) ruling (truncation indicator OUTSIDE the byte cell, preserving R-TUI-077's inertness-by-construction) — called the strongest passage in the artifact by one lane and verified across 19 input classes by another. THREE independent convergences (evidence deletion, withdrawn-indicator contradiction, id collapse) is the signal these are real defects, not reviewer taste. NONE of the six unbounded axes was in the original backlog carry, which described only 'one row per entry with no cap'. OPERATOR RULING: PIVOT — enforce the existing document _ByteBudget with per-variant fair share instead of capping cells and rows.

THREE INDEPENDENT CONVERGENCES, which is the signal these are real and not reviewer taste: (i) the two Phase-1 lanes DOUBLE-ALLOCATED the id space — 9-10 of 12 AT ids and ~26 of 40 TC ids bind to DIFFERENT observables (TC-453 is a D1 surface test in one artifact and a D2 rendering test in the other; 'fail-closed' is AT-171 in one and AT-170 in the other) — found by all three lanes separately; (ii) LLR-102.2's '>=' form is SATISFIED BY THE VERY DESIGN 00b M-6 refuted, because no LLR states partition-invariance or that _line_bytes is unchanged, so Phase 3 could implement the refuted non-composable form and pass every LLR and every AT, at an undercount LINEAR IN THE VARIANT COUNT (7 fixed emit batches + ~6 per variant) — strictly worse than the CRLF bug it replaces, which is bounded at N-2 and zero on Linux; (iii) D1's bounded-traversal LLR has no node that can go RED — measured, cap+break and cap+NO-break give IDENTICAL peaks (19019/19019, ratio 1.00) and wall time does not separate them either (1.00 vs 1.04). THREE OF THE FINDINGS ARE AGAINST ME, ALL ACCEPTED. (a) MY ID-REGISTRY FIX WAS INCOMPLETE: I fixed the RANGES before dispatch and claimed in the Phase-1 gate packet that the REV-4 collision was 'removed by construction'. Ranges were necessary and not sufficient — I never assigned per-id SEMANTICS, so both lanes filled the same range with different content. That claim is FALSIFIED and the correction is recorded. (b) MY M-7 RULING IS REFUTED: I diagnosed both lanes' D3 invariants as vacuous, then authored a third vacuous form. The qa lane built the minimal WRONG implementation (add report_bytes, leave write_text) and my ruled predicate passed 0 RED on a tree still writing CRLF. The critique is exact and I confirmed it by inspection: the predicate relates _line_bytes to report_bytes, BOTH pure functions of `lines`, so the writer never appears in the expression and no value it takes can depend on how bytes reach disk. 'Cannot bind pre-fix' is a property of the SYMBOL, not the DEFECT — the same argument would make `assert hasattr(rs, 'report_bytes')` a D3 gate. AT-174 re-classified as a regression PIN on the +1 convention (worth keeping — the C-26 census found _line_bytes has zero test refs) and explicitly NOT a D3 gate. (c) MY 'D2 CRASHES' FRAMING IS WRONG AT THE SHIPPED SURFACE: app.py:4034 CATCHES the ValueError; the tool declines with 'Report rejected: <CPython internals string>' in the OPERATOR-INPUT-REJECTION branch. My probe called generate_project_report directly, bypassing the handler — C-35 applied to me. The defect is real but is a report DENIAL plus a misclassified error that blames the operator for a Python-internals failure, not a crash; and the scope ruling's own justification ('two of them hang or crash the tool today') is therefore half wrong — D1 does, D2 does not. NEW SECURITY BLOCKERS, both HIGH, neither previously known: F1 the per-region cap re-introduces ATTACKER-SELECTABLE truncation and it is CLASS-SELECTIVE — the producer order at :1518/:1524/:1532 emits modification hits (100% attacker-supplied via the change file) before validation-issue hits (the tool's own findings, the evidence the addendum exists for), so 200 crafted entries evict 100% of that region's issue hits; the architect's Q-2 considered only per-region vs document-wide and concluded per-region avoids selectability — the selectability moved from the region axis to the hit-class axis, where it is worse. F2 the memory DoS is NOT closed by D1 and AT-164 is UNSATISFIABLE: _modifications_lines/_checklist_lines are uncapped at a measured 988 B/entry marginal, x64 the addendum's per-hit cost, so a CORRECT D1 fix leaves AT-164 RED — those two tables are exactly what batch-64 was deferred to bound, so the HLR overclaims across the batch boundary. CLEARED explicitly by security, worth recording: the write_bytes swap opens no new input path and changes no permission or overwrite semantics; flow_report_service's redaction posture is undisturbed (verified by blob sha, not grep, per the batch-62 false-positive lesson); no secret value anywhere. FOURTH CORRECTION AGAINST ME, from the security lane: my dispatch brief asserted that flow_report_service 'carries unredacted host paths in issue.message' as a consequence of batch-62 withdrawing D-11. FALSE — that file DOES redact absolute paths (batch-60 F2, redactor at :228 applied at :352/:371); the withdrawn D-11 control was the PROJECT-REPORT redactor at report_service.py:1048. I briefed a reviewer from memory of the wrong module and it checked rather than inherited the claim. F3 additionally: D2's bare-hex fallback is FORGEABLE as a decimal numeral — int('9'*3572,16) renders a Length cell of '9'x3572 with isdigit() True, understating the true length by ~10^730x in an evidentiary document, and AT-171's predicate ('non-empty, not -') tests less than its label; fold is to mandate a 0x prefix and assert it. ALSO: architect verified the flow_report_service scope ruling is load-bearing rather than scope creep (every claim checked at file:line) but flagged that widening past the operator's named scope was SELF-ruled, not referred. Phase-1 fold would be iteration 3 = the soft cap, so per the flow this is surfaced to the operator with the root cause named rather than silently looped.

decisions_log.decision: iterate-to-refine FOLD COMPLETE (iteration 3 of the soft cap) — one consolidated normative document; D1 re-scoped; 14 Before->After amendments discharge all 10 blockers
decisions_log.notes: OPERATOR RULINGS FOLDED: (a) 'fold completo con D1 re-alcanzado' at the 3-iteration cap escalation; (b) the missing id REGISTRY goes to BACKLOG as its own batch rather than being pulled into an already-overloaded batch. THE FOLD IS ONE DOCUMENT ON PURPOSE: parallel authorship WAS the root cause of the id collision, so re-dispatching two lanes to fix a collision caused by two lanes would reproduce it. 01-requirements-rescoped-consolidated.md is now the normative spec; both lane artifacts are retained on disk so the reversal stays traceable, and their executed transcripts remain cited evidence rather than being re-derived. THE OPERATOR'S DIAGNOSIS BEAT MINE AND IS NOW MEASURED (M-8): I attributed the collision to my own incomplete mitigation (fixed ranges, not per-id semantics). The operator said it recurs because there is no REGISTRY. Measured: 'the next free TC id' evaluates to 345 / 398 / 479 depending on whether you grep REQUIREMENTS.md, +tests/, or +.dev-flow/ — a 134-id spread, so two authors consulting different subsets BOTH believe they are in free space; that is the collision mechanism independent of anyone's carelessness. REQUIREMENTS.md registers 20 of 73 live AT ids (73% unregistered) and 97 of 188 live TC ids (52% unregistered), and carries 6 PHANTOM TC ids (319/320/324/325/326/327) that exist in NEITHER 'TC-NNN' nor 'def test_tcNNN' form — TC-319 being the exact node CLAUDE.md cites as the origin of control C-26, so the registry asserts a verifier that was removed without it noticing. I ALSO CORRECTED MY OWN MEASUREMENT MID-WAY: the first pass matched only TC-\d{3} while tests name functions test_tcNNN with no hyphen, so my input set was mis-derived — the same defect class I have been chasing all batch, committed while measuring it; re-run against both forms and the 6 phantoms survive both. D1 RE-SCOPED so it claims only what it delivers: per-HIT-CLASS cap (closes sec F1 — a per-region cap is a first-K cut in producer order and that order puts the 100%-attacker-supplied modification class FIRST and the tool's own validation findings LAST, executed at mods=200/cap=200 -> 0 of 5 issues survive, so the selectability moved from the region axis to the hit-class axis where it is worse); HLR-100 no longer asserts a document- or process-level memory bound (closes sec F2 — _modifications_lines/_checklist_lines are uncapped at a measured 988 B/entry, ~11x the addendum's 89 B/hit, so a CORRECT D1 fix left the old AT-164 RED); AT-164 WITHDRAWN as unsatisfiable-across-the-batch-boundary; bounded traversal now falsifiable by an injected COUNTING ITERABLE (closes arch B-2 / qa BLK-3 — cap+break and cap+NO-break gave identical peaks 19019/19019 ratio 1.00 and wall time did not separate them 1.00 vs 1.04); the <1.5 R-axis ratio WITHDRAWN because it false-fails a correct fix at a measured 1.89 (a per-region cap materialises RxCAP by construction). D2: the word 'crashes' removed — app.py:4034 CATCHES the ValueError and the tool declines with a CPython internals string in the OPERATOR-INPUT-REJECTION branch, so the defect is a report DENIAL plus an error that blames the operator for an internal failure; bare-hex fallback replaced by a mandatory 0x prefix (closes sec F3 — int('9'*3572,16) renders '9'x3572 with isdigit() True, understating the true length by ~10^730x in an evidentiary document and passing revision 2's 'non-empty, not -' predicate); acceptances now DERIVE the width from sys.get_int_max_str_digits() since the boundary moves with the interpreter (-X int_max_str_digits=1000 -> 831). D3: LLR-102.2 now states _line_bytes is UNCHANGED and partition-invariant and PROHIBITS redefining it in terms of the encoder — revision 2's '>=' form was satisfied by the very design M-6 refuted, which would have undercounted LINEARLY IN THE VARIANT COUNT (7 fixed emit batches + ~6 per variant), strictly worse than the CRLF bug it replaces; the retracted phrase removed from the heading; and the encoder is typed document_bytes(text: str) -> bytes, which serves BOTH writers without touching compose_flow_report's public -> str return covered by 39 tests (closes qa MAJ-2, verified at both call sites). AT-174 re-labelled a PIN on the +1 convention, explicitly NOT a D3 gate, after my own M-7 replacement was refuted. 3-increment cut, D3 first because AT-174's pin protects the accounting the other two rely on. OB-1 EXTENDED per sec F2: the PR must state batch-63 closes neither M-2 NOR the resident-memory axis. OB-2 NEW: the registry batch. OB-3: diff_report_service's two text-mode writers (no budget, so not D3) to BACKLOG. Zero production source mutated across the whole phase.

decisions_log.decision: RE-GATE: NOT-DISCHARGED (4 of 10 blockers genuinely closed). The fold was mine and it repeated the batch's own defect class in five new places — escalated to the operator rather than folded a fourth time
decisions_log.notes: Two independent auditors, each briefed to audit the discharge against the SOURCE REVIEWS rather than against my amendment table — the batch-62 distinction that found two majors a discharge matrix reported as closed. discharge-qa: NOT-DISCHARGED, 4 closed / 6 partial. security: OK-with-folds CONDITIONAL on an operator-signed risk acceptance for F2; without that signature, BLOCKED. GENUINELY CLOSED (4): arch B-1 via A-02 — LLR-102.2's 'byte-identical + redefinition prohibited' wording DOES exclude the refuted design, and the auditor executed that BOTH halves of the AT-174 pin are independently load-bearing (+1 -> +2 IS partition-invariant, so invariance alone would miss it, which is why the pin needs both clauses); arch B-2 / qa BLK-3 via A-08 — the counting iterable separates the arms, cap+break consumed 201 vs cap+NO-break 2000 at E=2000/K=200, so the counter CAN go RED where the resource-ratio form could not; sec F1's CROSS-CLASS half via A-07 — executed on the shipped producer order, per-region reproduces 0/5 and per-class gives 5/5. TWO DISCHARGES CLAIMED BUT NOT REAL, BOTH MINE. (1) A-14 -> sec F6: I never performed the narrowing. AT-170 still says 'on abort' and LLR-101.4 asserts 'a single terminal write, SO an abort leaves no file' as FACT — measured FALSE by both auditors independently, a mid-write OSError leaves a 100 000-200 000 byte file matching REPORT_FILENAME_REGEX. I wrote a requirement that asserts something the code does not honour, in the batch whose founding thesis is exactly that, while annotating it 'Covers F6's residue'. (2) A-01 -> the id collision: the COLLISION is closed but the CONDITION all three reviews attached is violated. All three said keep the union / drop nothing / add-don't-substitute. 8 of ~18 union observables now have NO node and 6 were dropped SILENTLY — including the one BOTH Phase-1 lanes independently agreed on (byte-identity below the cap, which leaves LLR-100.4 with ZERO acceptance) and the AST structural census the qa lane called 'the D3 gate CI can actually run', which arch B-4 explicitly said to ADD rather than substitute and I substituted. The entire 40-row TC layer was replaced by three id RANGES plus one TC-441. Consolidating to close a collision is not a licence to compress the layer that carries the coverage. FIVE NEW DEFECTS THE FOLD INTRODUCED: (a) TC-441's stated bound '<= 3K + eps' CONTRADICTS LLR-100.1's O(R x 3K) — executed R=2 -> 402, so it FALSE-FAILS a correct fix: BLK-4's failure mode re-entering through BLK-3's own amendment, i.e. I reintroduced the exact defect class I was closing, one amendment away from closing it; (b) AT-171 is UNSATISFIABLE on the constructible negative domain — ChangeSummaryEntry(0x2000, 0x1000) yields -4096 and past the digit limit the readable '-0x...' fails my 'starts with 0x' predicate, and sec F8 which named this was dropped in consolidation; the fix is ^-?0x[0-9A-F]+$; (c) AT-165 is structurally blind to intra-class and cross-variant eviction — GREEN in all three attacks in both auditors' probes, because its predicate tests the implementation's concatenation SHAPE, not the evidence: 200 attacker rows from v1 evict both tool findings from v2/v3, and 200 attacker-authored CHG-ADDRESS-SYNTAX warnings evict the ERROR-severity CHG-COLLISION 0/1; (d) N-1, no AT binds the SECOND LLR-101.1 site (report_service.py:1171, the checklist twin) — both source lanes HAD a checklist-twin AT and the consolidation dropped it; the two sites take DISJOINT inputs (change_summaries[].entries vs check_results[].entries) so a change-only fixture never reaches :1171, and AT-168/169/171 all pass with half the 'exact two-member set' unguarded; (e) AT-173's monkeypatch target is unstated and the obvious reading is VACUOUS because flow_report_service uses `from . import`, so rebinding report_service.document_bytes does not affect the already-bound name. SEC F2 = ACCEPTED RISK, NOT CLOSED, and it needs the operator's name rather than mine: stating a limitation removes the CLAIM, not the RISK. Verified the auditors' gap claim directly — BACKLOG.md:25 does carry the uncapped modifications/checklist tables, but frames them as a DOCUMENT-BYTE problem whose proposed _ByteBudget remedy does not bound RESIDENT memory, so the resident-memory axis specifically has no queue line; my consolidated doc's 'batch-64's subject' was an assertion with nothing behind it. Also dropped: OB-SEC-1, the git diff --numstat guard on the one cross-module edit (grep returns 0). SECURITY SELF-CORRECTED AGAINST ITS OWN PRIOR REVIEW, flagged loudly: its earlier F1 called the third addendum class 'the tool's own findings'; the code contradicts it — ChangeSummary.issues and CheckRunResult.issues are both list(document.issues) (changes/apply.py:363, changes/check.py:399), so ALL THREE classes are document-derived and the attacker controls every class's cardinality, which STRENGTHENS F1's residual. CLEARED and worth keeping: document_bytes is a pure str -> bytes with no new input path and NO new import edge (flow_report_service.py:69-74 already imports from .report_service and report_service.py:39-56 does not name it back, so no cycle; the change is +1 line in an existing tuple), identical 0o666 / truncate-on-open / PermissionError semantics, and flow_report_service's redaction posture verified UNCHANGED by blob sha (ad756ae0 == ad756ae0, 385b92ae == 385b92ae, git diff --numstat origin/main -- s19_app/ empty) rather than by grep. Phase 1 would now be at iteration 4. I committed at the previous gate to stop proposing folds at that point and bring the split option instead, so this is escalated, not folded. Zero production source mutated across every phase so far.

decisions_log.decision: Phase 3 CLOSED — D3-only shipped in ONE increment (4 files); 3 gates RED->GREEN, 2 pins green both sides by design
decisions_log.notes: Operator ruled D3-only at the re-gate escalation, then confirmed OB-4 and told me to run through to merge without stopping at each step. Revision 4 of the consolidated spec records the scope reduction and fixes the two rev-3 defects that were mine: AT-173's patch target (flow_report_service binds with `from .report_service import (...)`, so rebinding report_service.document_bytes leaves the module's own name untouched and the AT would pass against an unfixed writer — it now normatively patches flow_report_service.document_bytes, the patch-where-it-is-used rule) and the AST structural census RESTORED as AT-193 after rev-3 SUBSTITUTED it when the architect review had explicitly said to ADD it. AT-193's id was chosen carefully: AT-176 — which the discharge auditor called free — is actually used by 01-requirements-architect-rev5.md, the lane-A design carried to batch-64, and reusing an ambiguous id is the exact defect this batch is closing; AT-193 returns 0 hits across REQUIREMENTS.md, tests/, .dev-flow/ and docs/. IMPLEMENTATION IS 4 PRODUCTION LINES: document_bytes(text: str) -> bytes beside _line_bytes, both writers switched to write_bytes, +1 line in flow_report_service's EXISTING import tuple (so no new import edge and no cycle — security verified report_service does not name flow_report_service back). Typing the encoder on `str` rather than on `lines` is what makes one encoder serve both writers without touching compose_flow_report's public -> str return, which 39 tests cover. _line_bytes is UNCHANGED and its docstring now states why the +1 must not be re-derived from the encoder: the composer accounts in ~12 emit() batches so the accounting must be partition-invariant, and len(join) loses a byte per boundary. COUNTERFACTUAL CAPTURED BEFORE ANY PRODUCTION EDIT: 4 failed / 2 passed. The two passing are the AT-174 pins, and that is the SPECIFIED behaviour, not a gap — they pin _line_bytes, which the fix deliberately does not change; presenting them as evidence D3 was fixed would be this batch's own defect class. Post-fix 47 passed on the new + flow suites, ruff clean on all 4 files, frozen dual-guard 10 passed (C-27: source AND test-file guards, not one), report-adjacent derived observer set 116 passed. FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING: write_flow_report had ZERO tests — all 39 cases in test_flow_report_service.py exercise the pure compose_flow_report, so the writer was entirely uncovered, which is how D3 survived there unseen; AT-173 is the first test that touches it. REQUIREMENTS.md R-TUI-097 added, stating plainly that CI verifies this requirement's STRUCTURE and ARITHMETIC but not its platform-dependent BEHAVIOUR, because tui-ci and snapshot-regen both run ubuntu-latest where the unpatched writer already emits LF and the undercount is zero. BACKLOG reconciled with three new entries carrying full measurements: D1 returned (87-94 B/hit, product law on all three axes, and the two HIGH design constraints — per-class capping fixes cross-class 5/5 but NOT intra-class 0/1 or cross-variant 0/2, all three classes are document-derived so the attacker controls every cardinality, and bounding output does not bound traversal so only an injected counting iterable is falsifiable: 201 vs 2000); D2 returned (boundary 3572 but NOT stable, the AST-derived two-site set :996/:1171 with disjoint inputs, the shipped surface DENIES rather than crashes and misclassifies the error as operator input, and the eliminated-by-output candidates so they need not be re-argued); OB-2 the missing AT/TC registry with the 134-id spread and the 6 phantom TCs; OB-4 the resident-memory axis with its numbers, operator-confirmed as a carry rather than a signed risk acceptance because D3-only makes no memory claim to accept a residual against.
